title: Audio requirements
supports: Opened with WebFetch. RSS feed audio MP3 or AAC, AAC strongly recommended; bit rate ranges by mono or stereo and sample rate; loudness around -16 dB LKFS with +/-1 dB tolerance; true peak at or below -1 dBFS; measured per ITU-R BS.1770-5; apply loudness before encoding; WAV, FLAC or MP3 for subscriber audio, single-channel WAV or FLAC rejected; chapters recommended

title: Podcast RSS feed requirements
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Feed must follow RSS 2.0, be public and not password-protected, include itunes and content namespaces; hosting must allow HEAD and byte-range requests; unique enclosure with URL, length and type; GUID unique and never changes; ASCII URLs and file names; RFC 2822 dates; escaping special characters

title: Apple Podcasts Content Guidelines
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Metadata must represent content accurately; no search manipulation; impersonation rules; creators using AI for audio or video, including synthetic voices, AI hosts and replicas of real people, must disclose it prominently in content and metadata; AI must not mislead; rights to all content; explicit tag; editorial must greatly exceed advertising; ads must follow the law

title: Transcripts on Apple Podcasts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Automatic transcripts after publishing; creators can supply VTT or SRT through the RSS transcript tag; VTT can name speakers; quality standards; episodes over 10 hours may not be transcribed; supported languages; labels for automatic and provided transcripts; none for episodes only in private feeds

title: Chapters on Apple Podcasts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Automatic chapters from iOS 26.2 for English full and bonus episodes of 10 minutes or more; own chapters in the description from 00:00:00 with at least three, through the podcast:chapters tag, or in MP4 or ID3 metadata; best practice of three or more chapters, no more than six per hour, each at least two minutes, titles under 45 characters and fewer than five words

title: How to set the order of podcast episodes
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Episodic versus serial show types; seasons; episode numbers belong in metadata fields or RSS tags, not titles; how trailers and bonus episodes are placed

title: Make the next great podcast trailer
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Three kinds of trailer; keep trailers to two minutes or less; a four-part outline ending with when new episodes arrive and a reminder to follow

title: Search on Apple Podcasts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Search ranking draws on metadata, popularity and engagement; ratings and reviews are not used in Search ranking; distinctive names; avoid emojis and repeated episode titles; promote at launch

title: Analytics
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Definitions of listeners, engaged listeners (at least 20 minutes or 40% of an episode), plays, time listened, average consumption and followers; data shows only with at least five unique listeners; default 60-day range

title: Episode chapters
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Automatic chapters (English only, not all shows); manual chapters as timestamps in the description, first at 00:00, at least 3 chapters, at least 30 seconds apart, plain-text titles, titles under 40 characters recommended; Podlove chapters in RSS for shows hosted elsewhere; AI chapter hooks can be turned off

title: Managing episode transcripts on Spotify
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Some shows get automatic transcripts; edit by downloading the VTT and re-uploading; own VTT or SRT up to 5MB with timestamps; turning on automatic transcripts replaces an uploaded one; option to distribute transcripts by RSS

title: Video specs
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Video podcast specs: MP4 recommended, H.264 or H.265, 1080p or higher recommended, 16:9 recommended with no added borders, 24 to 60 fps, AAC-LC audio at 128 kbps or more in stereo, file under 10 GB recommended (up to 60 GB), under 4 hours recommended (up to 12)

title: Spotify for Creators community guidelines
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Impersonation intended or likely to deceive is not allowed; content provided without rightsholder permission may be removed; samples should be cleared; spam rules; policies may change

title: Podcasts on YouTube delivered by RSS feed (help article 13525207)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. YouTube makes videos from RSS episodes using show art as a static image; new episodes upload automatically and first as private; edits and re-uploaded audio do not sync; no < > or HTML in titles and descriptions; podcast content cannot contain advertisements, and branded content, sponsorships or endorsements must be declared; ownership verified by a code sent to the feed email; select countries only

title: Disclosing use of altered or synthetic content
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Realistic altered or synthetic content must be disclosed under AI use in YouTube Studio, such as making a real person appear to say something they did not; cloning your own voice for voice-overs or dubs and AI help with scripts or titles are listed as not needing disclosure

title: Celebrating 1 billion monthly podcast users on YouTube (26 Feb 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. More than 1 billion monthly active viewers of podcast content on YouTube as of January 2025; over 400 million hours of podcasts watched monthly on living-room devices in 2024; YouTube citing Edison Research as the most used US podcast service

title: FTC Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Paid hosts giving positive opinions are endorsers; disclose payment the audience would not expect, at the start of a segment and when products are endorsed, in plain words rather than vague ones; an audible endorsement needs at least an audible disclosure; you cannot describe experience with a product you have not tried; Guides revised in 2023

title: CAP Code section 2: Recognition of marketing communications
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Rule 2.1 marketing must be obviously identifiable; rule 2.3 commercial intent must be made clear; rule 2.4 advertorials labelled; rules 2.3 and 2.4 reflect DMCCA Schedule 20 prohibited practices

title: Influencer Legal Hub
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Advertising, brand partnerships, paid content and affiliate marketing must be disclosed; Unfair Commercial Practices Directive and Digital Services Act listed; the hub lists national guidance, including a Norwegian Consumer Authority guideline on marketing in podcasts

title: AI Act Article 50: Transparency obligations
publisher: AI Act Service Desk, European Commission
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Deployers must disclose audio, image or video deepfakes; for evidently artistic, creative, satirical or fictional work, disclose the existence of generated content without hampering the work; providers mark synthetic output in a machine-readable way; information given at first exposure

title: AI Act Article 113: Entry into force and application
publisher: AI Act Service Desk, European Commission
supports: Opened with WebFetch. General application date of 2 August 2026, which covers Article 50 (Chapter IV is not among the listed exceptions, so this is read from the structure); page based on the consolidated text as at 27 July 2026 with Digital Omnibus amendments marked

title: Professional Voice Cloning
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Professional voice clones are for your own voice only, confirmed by a voice verification step; the FAQ says you cannot clone someone else's voice even with their consent; samples must be one speaking voice. The page header carries instructions aimed at AI agents (fetch llms.txt), which were not followed

title: Engage: musicians
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A recording can contain two works, the musical work and the sound recording, commonly owned and licensed separately; use needs public domain status, permission or licence, or an exception such as fair use; no set minimum amount; failing to reach the owner is not permission; publishers and performing rights organisations often handle licensing

title: About CC licenses
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Six licences, all needing credit; NC allows noncommercial use only; ND allows no adaptations; SA requires adaptations under the same terms

title: Understanding SC 1.2.1: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Level A: prerecorded audio-only content needs a text alternative such as a transcript, unless it is a labelled media alternative for text; a transcript records what is said, who says it and significant sounds; page updated 6 Sep 2026

title: R 128: Loudness normalisation and permitted maximum level of audio signals
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Broadcast programme loudness target of -23 LUFS; version 5.0 published 21 Nov 2023

title: RSS 2.0 Specification
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Version 2.0.11 (30 Mar 2009), frozen; required channel elements title, link and description; enclosure needs url, length and type; guid and isPermaLink; pubDate in RFC 822 format

title: podcast:transcript tag
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Transcript tag under item with required url and type, optional language and rel=captions; formats VTT, SRT, JSON, HTML and plain text; several tags allowed per episode

title: Podcast Measurement Technical Guidelines
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Version 2.3 released September 2026, page updated 29 Sep 2026; podcast measurement is based on server logs; a compliance programme lets companies show they follow the guidelines

title: Podcasts as a source of news and information (18 Apr 2023)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. About half of US adults listened to a podcast in the past year; survey of 5,132 US adults on the American Trends Panel, 5 to 11 Dec 2022; comedy, entertainment and politics the most common topics
